newsitem.title: UK: Hume assails IRA "blind alley" violence.
newsitem.headline: Hume assails IRA "blind alley" violence.

text.p: John Hume, a prominent Northern Ireland Catholic leader, challenged the IRA's Sinn Fein political arm on Thursday to demand an end to the guerrillas' war against British rule.

The leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) also signalled that he was not prepared to continue talking indefinitely to Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams in the shadow of Irish Republican Army resurgence.

In a hard-hitting newspaper article in the Belfast-based Irish News, he said the Republican Movement, which comprises Sinn Fein and the IRA, had led their supporters down a "blind alley of violence" for more than 25 years.
Hume, whose party is the chief voice of minority Irish nationalists, has held a series of talks with Adams, but late last year Britain spurned their ideas for achieving a truce.
He accused his republican rivals of electoral fraud and intimidation in "their bid to win the leadership of northern (Ireland) nationalism.

"If the Sinn Fein leadership truly believe in what they say, then they must join with me today in publicly calling on the IRA for an immediate and unconditional end to a war which, by their own admission, has no purpose and cannot resolve this conflict or produce a lasting peace," Hume wrote.

In a development that political analysts said marked a significant shift, Hume signalled that his peace-brokering talks with Adams must achieve an IRA truce within a time limit, which he did not specify.

Hume declared that he had backed Sinn Fein's proposal that any future all-party peace talks on the province's future should be held within "an indicative time frame" to prevent discussions dragging on interminably.

"I believe the same considerations apply to our dialogue about creating a ceasefire. It would be unreasonable to expect me and my party to go on, month in and month out, going over the same arguments endlessly. "Ninety-five per cent of the people of this island want a ceasefire now...We have a democratic right to demand a ceasefire from the IRA and to set a time frame within which the questions must be resolved."
Hume said that Sinn Fein had "availed of our good faith as honest brokers (and)...now intend to cast us aside, using any means fair or foul."
The IRA says it will not call a truce before Britain has a new government in an election due by late May.
Sinn Fein said an electoral pact with the SDLP could result in Catholics doubling their representation by winning eight of Northern Ireland's 18 seats in the British parliament.
But Hume, whose SDLP has four members in parliament, rejected the deal.
"To make an electoral pact with Sinn Fein without an IRA ceasefire would be the equivalent of asking our voters to support the killing of innocent human beings by the IRA".
Late last year Hume had urged British Prime Minister John Major to assure Sinn Fein speedy entry to all-party talks after an IRA truce.

Major accused Sinn Fein of crying crocodile tears about IRA violence and said he would be guided by intelligence agency assessments of the credibility of any future truce before giving Sinn Fein a voice in talks.
